component: scripts/hardware_profile.py + adoption/hardware-profiles.json (new tool, no prior pin; this is a fix-round receipt superseding the first hardware-profile-tool.json after an independent Opus review)
to_version: unreleased, added in this unit (claude/w2-hw-profiles-20260923), revised after review

preregistration.written_after_fix_note: Written after implementing the review's fixes and before re-running the checks below, not before the fix itself; this is an honest amendment round, not the original preregistration (see mlx-lm-hash-lock.json for the same disclosure pattern this receipt follows).
preregistration.expectation: After the fixes below, a run on this WSL host will report effective_ram_gb from /proc/meminfo (47.0), not the .wslconfig ceiling (48.0), which moves embedding_semantic_rag_tier from 'full' to 'standard' (>=32, <48). cpu_brand will be populated from /proc/cpuinfo ('Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 275HX') instead of asserted. ecosystem_bounded_run output will report named ecosystem_job_memory_high_gb/ecosystem_job_memory_max_gb (not a single unnamed ceiling), sized as max(default_max_gb=6, round(ram*0.25,1)) capped at 32, i.e. 11.8/7.9 on this host. local_generation_model_tier stays 'large-32b-q4' (discrete GPU path is unaffected by the macOS unified-memory fraction fix). tests.test_hardware_profile passes, including new coverage for detect_nvidia_gpu (mocked _run), measure_macos (mocked _run), the WSL RAM-source precedence (_effective_ram_gb), and multi-.wslconfig ambiguity (_find_all_wslconfigs).
preregistration.criteria: python3 scripts/hardware_profile.py exits 0 and its JSON 'recommended'/'measured' blocks match every value above exactly; python3 -m unittest tests.test_hardware_profile passes all cases (33, up from 16).

acceptance_check_ref: tests/test_hardware_profile.py (this unit's suite, extended in this fix round); prior receipt (this file's previous revision, git history) recorded the pre-fix behavior this review found wrong.
commands: python3 scripts/hardware_profile.py --out evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260923/hw-profiles/this-host.json (then the Windows username in wslconfig_source was redacted to 'example'; see this-host.json's _redaction_note)
results: this-host.json (post-fix) measured: cores=24, cpu_brand='Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 275HX' (now actually read from /proc/cpuinfo, not asserted), ram_gb_proc_meminfo=47.0, wslconfig_memory_gb=48.0 (wslconfig_memory_gb_evidence_class='source_review'), effective_ram_gb=47.0 (effective_ram_gb_source='proc_meminfo'), wslconfig_other_candidates=[] (only one Windows user profile found), gpu={name: 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU', vram_gb: 23.9}, is_wsl=true.

recommended (post-fix): workflow_concurrency_cap=16 (unchanged), local_generation_model_tier='large-32b-q4' (unchanged; discrete GPU path), embedding_semantic_rag_tier='standard' (changed from 'full': 47.0 < 48 threshold), concurrent_use_warning=null (only set for the macOS unified-memory path), ecosystem_job_memory_max_gb=11.8, ecosystem_job_memory_high_gb=7.9 (replacing the single unnamed ecosystem_bounded_run_memory_gb=24.0 field) -- matches the preregistered expectation exactly.

unittest: 'Ran 33 tests in 0.114s / OK' (16 original synthetic-input cases plus 17 new: DetectNvidiaGpuTests x4, MeasureMacosTests x3, EffectiveRamGbTests x3, CpuinfoParsingTests x2, WslConfigAmbiguityTests x3, plus 2 additional RecommendTests cases for the concurrent_use_warning and discrete-GPU paths).
limits: Measured on exactly one host (this laptop); the 128GB WSL workstation and macOS entries in adoption/hardware-profiles.json remain labelled_projection, not native_proven, until each is actually run.

The macos_unified_gpu_working_set_fraction (0.6) is a labelled, conservative assumption, not a measurement -- no macOS host was available in this worktree to measure actual Metal working-set behavior.

The ecosystem_job_memory_high_gb/max_gb sizing rule (max_fraction_of_ram=0.25, ceiling_max_gb=32) is this unit's own bounded-fraction judgment call reacting to the review's finding that the old rule (half of RAM, unnamed) was four times the wrapper's own MemoryMax default; it is not validated against an actual WSL-stability stress test at the new ceiling.
No GPU/model workload is actually executed by this script; tiers are threshold recommendations, not measured throughput.

_find_all_wslconfigs's multi-user ambiguity fix only reports the other candidates found; it still picks the alphabetically-first one automatically rather than requiring an explicit choice, since no signal (e.g. the active WSL distro's owning Windows user) is read to disambiguate without invoking a Windows binary.
